PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PREPARED AT THE REQUEST OF COUNSEL

TO: Deal Team / Engagement File
FROM: [Associate]
RE: Counterparty Markup Analysis — Draft NSA and Supporting Materials
DATE: [Current Date]

================================================================================
RISK-PRIORITIZED MARKUP ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
================================================================================

I. SCOPE AND MATERIALS REVIEWED

This memorandum reviews the counterparty's markup of the draft NSA (the "Draft NSA")
against the base materials filed in this matter's folder. In accordance with the
engagement instruction, I identified and read in full every document relevant to this
engagement and reconciled all sources that touch the marked provisions.

Relevant documents reviewed:
- Base materials (Draft NSA and negotiating record): the operative agreement and its
  representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification
  and termination provisions, together with counsel's flagged open issues.
- Counterparty markup: the counterparty's revision of the Draft NSA.
- Schedules and exhibits: Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2
  (retained liabilities), and Exhibit B (survival matrix).
- Deal team correspondence: the controlling partner instruction governing concession
  priorities.
- One document identified as misfiled/unrelated administrative correspondence and
  affirmatively excluded from reliance.

In accordance with the schedules and exhibits instruction and the governing deal-team
correspondence, the analysis below reconciles BOTH the counterparty markup and the
scheduled exceptions against the base materials, and gives effect only to the latest
controlling partner instruction (which supersedes any conflicting earlier message in
the thread).

================================================================================
II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF DEVIATIONS AND RISK RANKING
================================================================================

The counterparty's markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three
material changes. Each is assessed below against (a) the base materials, (b) the
scheduled exceptions in Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2 and Exhibit B, and (c) the
controlling deal-team instruction. Findings are ranked by risk severity:

    RISK       DEVIATION                                       RECOMMENDATION
    --------   ---------------------------------------------   ------------------------------
    HIGH       New limitation period shortens survival of      REJECT — treat as walk-away
               core representations, contradicting Exhibit B   (client instruction); do not
               (survival matrix).                              concede.
    HIGH       Indemnification cap silently reduced and        REJECT / COUNTER — restore cap
               basket converted from deductible to tipping,    and retain true deductible;
               silently shifting Schedule 5.2 retained         counter at approved fallback;
               liabilities.                                    quantify exposure.
    MEDIUM     MAE definition adds carve-outs for regulatory   COUNTER — narrow carve-outs to
               action intersecting Schedule 3.7 pending        exclude the kind of inquiries
               regulatory inquiries.                           disclosed; require materiality.

================================================================================
III. MATERIAL CHANGE 1 — SURVIVAL (HIGH RISK; WALK-AWAY POSITION)
================================================================================

A. What the counterparty did
The markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core
representations relative to the base materials.

B. Reconciliation against base materials and supporting schedules
- The base materials' Exhibit B sets a survival matrix prescribing the survival
  periods for the core (and other) representations. The markup's shortened limitation
  period directly contradicts the survival matrix in Exhibit B.
- Under the schedules-and-exhibits instruction, Exhibit B controls over general
  statements in the base contracts materials. The shortened survival therefore cannot
  stand without a conforming change to the governing survival matrix, which the
  counterparty has not made.
- The controlling deal-team correspondence states that the client "treats any
  survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue." This is the operative, latest
  instruction and supersedes any contrary earlier message.

C. Risk assessment
Shortened survival for core representations materially reduces the client's window to
assert post-closing claims on the most important representations. Because the
deviation contradicts the contractual survival matrix (Exhibit B) and exceeds the
client's explicit risk tolerance, this is a walk-away item. If conceded, it would cap
the practical value of the indemnity regime at the shortened limitation period.

D. Recommendation
REJECT the survival-period reduction. Hold the Exhibit B survival matrix without
change. Do not propose a counter that concedes any shortening of the core
representation survival periods. If the counterparty insists, elevate per governance —
this is outside approved fallbacks and will not be accepted.

E. Counter-draft language
Delete the markup's replacement limitation-period language and restore the Exhibit B
survival matrix by returning the operative survival provision to:

    "Survival. The representations and warranties of [Party] set forth in this
    Agreement shall survive the Closing for the periods set forth on Exhibit B
    (Survival Matrix). For the avoidance of doubt, the survival periods for the
    core representations shall be no shorter than those set forth on Exhibit B, and
    no earlier expiration of the applicable limitation period shall apply."

================================================================================
IV. MATERIAL CHANGE 2 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP AND BASKET (HIGH RISK; COUNTER)
================================================================================

A. What the counterparty did
The markup (i) silently reduces the indemnification cap and (ii) converts the basket
from a true deductible to a tipping basket.

B. Reconciliation against base materials and supporting schedules
- The base materials provide a stated indemnification cap and a true deductible
  basket (recovery only for covered losses in excess of the basket).
- Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. The markup's indemnification changes would
  silently shift those retained liabilities to the indemnifying party by (i) lowering
  the cap (so the shifted liability crowds out other recoveries) and (ii) converting
  the basket to a tipping basket (so losses become recoverable from the first dollar
  once the threshold is met, changing the allocation of the excluded band).
- The controlling deal-team correspondence states the client "will concede the basket
  conversion." The client has therefore authorized concession of the deductible-to-
  tipping conversion mechanics. This concession is within approved fallback parameters
  and does not require further escalation solely on the basket mechanics question.

C. Risk assessment
The cap reduction increases the counterparty's exposure ceiling exposure management
risk and, combined with the silent shift of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities,
materially reallocates post-closing risk. The basket conversion alone is a conceded
point under the controlling instruction, but the cap reduction — which crowds out and
effectively reinstates exposure for retained liabilities that Schedule 5.2 assigns to
the client — is not authorized and must be resisted.

D. Recommendation
- Accept the basket conversion only to the extent mechanics-only and within the client's
  expressed concession (no change to the excluded-band economics beyond the conversion
  itself).
- REJECT / COUNTER the cap reduction. Restore the cap to the base-materials level, and
  obtain the approved fallback value as the maximum concession. Confirm that Schedule
  5.2 retained liabilities remain excluded and are not silently pulled into the
  indemnified bucket by a lower cap.
- Quantify exposure at the applicable run-rate to support the escalation/approval
  record for any movement below the base cap.

E. Counter-draft language
Basket (counterparty's conceded mechanics, with excluded band preserved):
    "Indemnification Basket. The Indemnifying Party shall have no liability under
    this Article unless and until the aggregate amount of covered Losses exceeds the
    Basket (the 'Basket'), as set forth below. Once the aggregate amount of covered
    Losses exceeds the Basket, the Indemnifying Party shall be liable for all covered
    Losses from the first dollar; provided that the Basket described in this
    sentence shall in no event operate to shift, reduce or reallocate any retained
    liability identified on Schedule 5.2."

Cap (counter to restore base level):
    "Cap. The aggregate liability of the Indemnifying Party for all covered Losses
    under this Article shall not exceed the Cap set forth below, which Cap shall be
    measured in accordance with the base materials and shall not be reduced by the
    existence of any retained liability identified on Schedule 5.2."

================================================================================
V. MATERIAL CHANGE 3 — MAE CARVE-OUTS (MEDIUM RISK; COUNTER)
================================================================================

A. What the counterparty did
The markup revises the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" (MAE) to add
carve-outs for regulatory action.

B. Reconciliation against base materials and supporting schedules
- Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. The markup's new carve-outs
  for regulatory action are drafted to sweep in "regulatory action of the kind" at
  issue in this matter — i.e., precisely the two pending inquiries in Schedule 3.7.
- Adding carve-outs that exempt regulatory-driven events from the definition of MAE
  would insulate the counterparty from a condition/precondition tied to MAE, and would
  leave the client without the protections the base materials intended for
  Schedule 3.7-type exposure.
- The scheduled exceptions (Schedule 3.7) qualify the base materials and control over
  general statements; the markup's carve-outs contradict the intended treatment of the
  disclosed inquiries.

C. Risk assessment
The MAE carve-out revision is material because it reaches the specific regulatory
inquiries already disclosed on Schedule 3.7, effectively exempting the very exposure
the base materials were negotiated to protect against. It is medium priority relative
to the survival (walk-away) and cap issues but still must be resisted or narrowed.

D. Recommendation
REJECT the broad carve-out as drafted. Counter with language narrowing any regulatory
carve-out to exclude (i) the kind of inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7; (ii) events
arising from the counterparty's own non-consent or failure to cooperate; and (iii)
regulatory action that has a demonstrably material adverse effect regardless of
source. Any carve-out must be subject to a materiality qualifier.

E. Counter-draft language
    "MAE Exceptions. An event, change, development or effect shall not constitute or
    be deemed to constitute a Material Adverse Effect if it results from [insert
    standard general exceptions]; provided, however, that such exceptions shall not
    apply to, and shall not exclude, any event, change, development or effect arising
    out of or relating to (i) any regulatory inquiry, investigation or proceeding of
    the kind disclosed on Schedule 3.7 or otherwise then pending against the Company,
    (ii) any action taken or not taken at the direction or with the consent of the
    counterparty, or (iii) any such event, change, development or effect that, in the
    good-faith determination of the non-affected party, has a material adverse effect
    on the business, financial condition or results of operations of the Company
    irrespective of its source."

================================================================================
VI. DEVIATION MATRIX AND PRIORITIZED ACTION ITEMS
================================================================================

    #   Provision         Counterparty change            Risk     Recommendation
    --  ----------------  ----------------------------   ------   -------------------------
    1   Survival           Shortened limitation period   HIGH     REJECT (walk-away); restore
                          contradicts Exhibit B matrix             Exhibit B survival matrix.
    2   Indemnification   Cap reduced; basket            HIGH     Concede basket mechanics;
       cap / basket       converted deductible->tipping            counter/reject cap; restore
                                                                   cap; exclude Schedule 5.2.
    3   MAE definition     Adds regulatory carve-outs     MEDIUM   Counter; narrow carve-outs to
                           intersecting Schedule 3.7               exclude disclosed inquiries;
                                                                   require materiality qualifier.

================================================================================
VII. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

Of the three material changes in the counterparty markup, the survival-period
reduction is the controlling priority (HIGH) and is a walk-away item under the latest
deal-team instruction; it must be rejected and the Exhibit B survival matrix retained.
The indemnification cap reduction is also HIGH and must be countered to restore the
base cap while conceding only the basket-conversion mechanics the client has already
authorized, ensuring Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities are not silently shifted. The
MAE carve-outs are MEDIUM priority and should be narrowed to exclude the kind of
regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7, with a materiality qualifier.

Counter-draft language for each material change is set forth above for incorporation
into the responsive redline. All recommendations reflect the controlling (latest)
deal-team instruction; the conflicting superseded instruction and the misfiled
unrelated correspondence were excluded from reliance.

This memorandum is privileged and confidential, prepared in anticipation of
negotiation and for the client's internal decision-making.
